title: Antipatterns: the PowerPoint architect, the ivory tower and overengineering

videos.script: This course has spent sixteen lessons describing the job. This one describes how it goes wrong. {{mirror}} Each failure starts as a reasonable habit, taken too far. {{slide}} The PowerPoint architect draws the system as it should be, and stops looking at the system as it is. The slides get better. The code drifts away from them. {{tower}} The ivory tower decides far from the teams who live with the decisions. Nobody argues. Nobody follows, either. {{overbuilt}} Overengineering builds for a future nobody asked for. Every extra piece has to be run, upgraded and understood, long after the reason has gone. {{door}} Two more, briefly: the gatekeeper, who approves everything and becomes the queue. And the absent architect, where nobody decides and the system ends up shaped by accident. {{map}} For each one you will see the symptoms, the causes, the cost and the alternative. Then the questions give you situations from Carreto. Name the antipattern, and say what Renata should have done instead.
